sites.name: ADVANCED BASE DEPOT-RIFLE RANGE

facts.summary: A military history page says the Navy originally acquired the Oxnard Seacoast Battery site as part of a 325-acre lease approved on 3 December 1942. The page lists 'Advanced Base Depot - Rifle Range' as one of several other names for the training area. It does not say the rifle range was a separate facility, so the link to this FUDS record is an alias match only.
facts.authority: Ventura Group, Harbor Defenses of Los Angeles history page (militarymuseum.org)
facts.reference: Oxnard Tactical Battery 3 (Camp Rousseau; Military Training Area, Oxnard Shores)
facts.quote: The Navy originally acquired the site known as the Oxnard Seacoast Battery as part of a 325 acre lease

facts.summary: By March 1948 the Navy canceled the leases for the 325 acres, including the 19-acre battery site. The same page treats the rifle range as an alias for the whole training area, so the record's 342.3-acre figure is not checked against this lease.
facts.authority: Ventura Group, Harbor Defenses of Los Angeles history page (militarymuseum.org)
facts.reference: Oxnard Tactical Battery 3 (Camp Rousseau; Military Training Area, Oxnard Shores)
facts.quote: By March 1948, the Navy canceled the leases for the 325 acres, including the 19 acre battery site area.

gaps: No Ventura County Assessor portal could be verified. Both URLs tried returned a 'Request Rejected' page, and no other assessor URL was confirmed, so no portal is listed.
The USACE California FUDS inventory PDF and the USACE site could not be opened, so the inventory row for this record was not checked directly.
The history page does not separate the rifle range from the seacoast battery, so this record may describe a different parcel. The 1942 and 1948 facts are alias matches only.
Oxnard permit, code-enforcement and planning records were not searched, so permit and zoning history is unknown.
The record has no address and no atlas parcel id, so no parcel-level owner, deed or tax check was possible.

sites.name: CAMP HOWZE

facts.summary: The Texas State Historical Association handbook says Camp Howze was located on a 59,000-acre tract purchased from local landowners beginning in December 1941. The record's acreage is 58,702.8.
facts.authority: Texas State Historical Association, Handbook of Texas (camp history entry)
facts.reference: Camp Howze: A Historical Overview of the WWII Infantry Training Camp
facts.quote: It was located on a 59,000-acre tract purchased from local landowners beginning in December 1941

facts.summary: The same handbook entry says the camp was declared surplus, disbanded and leveled in 1946. It says nothing about what happened to the land after that.
facts.authority: Texas State Historical Association, Handbook of Texas (camp history entry)
facts.reference: Camp Howze: A Historical Overview of the WWII Infantry Training Camp
facts.quote: In 1946 the camp was declared surplus, disbanded, and leveled.

gaps: No Cooke County Appraisal District portal could be verified. The two domains tried did not resolve, so no assessor or tax URL is listed.
The USACE Fort Worth District Camp Howze page returned HTTP 403, so its 31,132-acre Maneuver Area figure and its munitions statement could not be checked.
The atlas owner list (City of Gainesville / Moss Lake and private owners) was not verified. The Moss Lake link is unconfirmed, and no parcel was searched.
No Cooke County deed, lien or tax record was checked, and the atlas parcel id is null.
The handbook says nothing about what happened to the land after 1946, so no post-closure ownership fact is recorded.

sites.name: MATHIS BROTHERS LANDFILL (SOUTH MARBLE TOP ROAD)

portals.name: Walker County, Georgia government site (Assessors Office; links to qPublic Property Records Search)
portals.note: Opened. The homepage links to a qPublic Property Records Search under the Assessors Office. That search's own URL was not confirmed, and it was not opened. The page does not state a fee for the search.

portals.name: Walker County Tax Commissioner (linked from the county site)
portals.note: Named as the Tax Commissioner link on walkercountyga.gov. Not opened. Tax status is unknown.

facts.summary: EPA's site profile says a landfill operated on this site from 1974 to 1980, and the site is about 10 acres.
facts.reference: MATHIS BROTHERS LANDFILL (SOUTH MARBLE TOP ROAD), EPA ID GAD980838619
facts.quote: It includes an area where a landfill operated from 1974 to 1980.

facts.summary: EPA's site profile says the site was placed on the National Priorities List in 1989 because of contaminated debris, groundwater and soil from the landfill.
facts.reference: MATHIS BROTHERS LANDFILL (SOUTH MARBLE TOP ROAD), EPA ID GAD980838619
facts.quote: EPA placed the site on the Superfund program's National Priorities List (NPL) in 1989

facts.summary: EPA's site profile says EPA, Georgia EPD and the site's responsible party continue to protect people and the environment through groundwater monitoring, site inspections and Five-Year Reviews. The page gives no date for this status and no reuse or land-use statement.
facts.reference: MATHIS BROTHERS LANDFILL (SOUTH MARBLE TOP ROAD), EPA ID GAD980838619
facts.quote: EPA, Georgia EPD and the site's PRP continue to protect people and the environment

gaps: The 2000 Federal Register notice on the Velsicol cost-recovery settlement (about $4 million, covering this site and two others) redirected off-domain and was not opened. No settlement fact is recorded.
The Walker County qPublic property search was not opened, so no parcel, owner, deed, lien or tax record for this site was checked.
The Walker County Tax Commissioner site was not opened, so tax status is unknown.
The atlas owner and parcel id are null. Matching to a parcel was not possible.

The EPA profile in the fetch had no current cleanup-status date and no reuse statement. A search summary that describes a property owner with agricultural, industrial or commercial reuse interest is undated and was not verified, so it is not recorded.
Sources differ on the town. EPA and the Federal Register place the site in Kensington, while some listings say Lafayette. The record's city is Kensington, so it was used.

sites.name: PEOPLES GAS CRAWFORD STATION FORMER MGP

portals.name: Cook County Assessor's Office advanced property search
portals.note: Opened. The page offers an advanced search by address, PIN or neighborhood. The page does not mention a fee or login for this search. No search was run for the treated parcels.

portals.name: Cook County Treasurer
portals.note: Opened. The homepage does not show a PIN or address tax search. It describes paying property taxes with no fee and has an electronic billing login. No tax record was checked.

portals.name: Cook County Clerk, Recordings Division
portals.note: Opened. The homepage describes the Recordings Division as maintaining land records but does not name an online search. No deed or lien search was run.

facts.summary: EPA's site profile says Peoples Gas completed in situ stabilization treatment on Parcels A and B in late January 2025, after more than 224,700 tons of soil were removed. The profile says cleanup and investigations are ongoing.
facts.reference: PEOPLES GAS CRAWFORD STATION FORMER MGP, EPA ID ILN000510192
facts.quote: In late January 2025, Peoples Gas completed in situ stabilization (ISS) treatment activities at Parcels "A" and "B"

facts.summary: A 2021 Block Club Chicago article says the Peoples Gas Crawford Station at 4358 W. 35th Place will have 4 to 8 feet of contaminated soil removed and taken off-site, with a cleanup expected to last about a year. The address differs from the EPA profile's 3500 South Pulaski Road.
facts.reference: Peoples Gas Will Start Remediating Former Manufactured Gas Plant In Little Village Next Month, Aug 16, 2021
facts.quote: it will remove 4-8 feet of contaminated soil.

facts.summary: EPA's site profile places the Crawford Station former manufactured gas plant site at 3500 South Pulaski Road in Chicago. The page gives no date for this statement.
facts.reference: PEOPLES GAS CRAWFORD STATION FORMER MGP, EPA ID ILN000510192
facts.quote: The Crawford Station former manufactured gas plant (MGP) site is located at 3500 South Pulaski Road in Chicago, Illinois.

gaps: The 2012 EPA administrative order on consent for this site was seen only in a search summary and was not on the fetched profile page, so it is not recorded as a fact.

The address is inconsistent across sources: 3500 South Pulaski Road (EPA profile), 4358 W. 35th Place (2021 news) and 4543 W. 35th Street / 3600 S. Kostner Avenue for the treated parcels (search summary only). Parcel-level matching is therefore unresolved.
No Cook County Assessor search was run for the treated parcels, so owner, deed, lien and tax history are unknown.
Chicago building, demolition and environmental permit records were not searched.
The EPA profile gave no 2026 status. The most recent dated milestone is January 2025, and the status should be checked with EPA Region 5.
The atlas parcel id is null, so no parcel-level owner check was possible.
